checked.why:
I traced the whole road at HEAD. HEAD changes nothing in scripts/ against b5a29e73, and calls.mjs's last commit is 7450e430. On the sheet, the only gates on Support are the price, Experience and alreadyArmed, and none of those apply to Support. callBarred and hopeCallRefusal stop a Hope Call only for the Eclipse, the Overflow's Silence, death and the Silence Call. allowed-now.mjs:92 shuts callHope only in an Eclipse, so Support can be bought while a mask stands, both during the fight and after it (the mask outlives the incident: owner-115 STATUS item 1b). Support's target is "player" (config.mjs:2322), so pickTarget calls pickPlayer (call-pickers.mjs:242). pickPlayer draws its labels with nameAsSeen but returns the actor object itself. runCall passes that choice to confirmCall unchanged (sheet-actions.mjs:908-929). confirmCall prints describeChoice(choice), which returns choice.target.name, the real name. No card is posted, so secret.mjs wordsFor never reads this text.

Nothing in the tests or papers pins the opposite or accepts it:
- R7404 checks only that six picker files contain "nameAsSeen(" and that the Frisk's ask is cut. It never reads calls.mjs.
- No test or scenario mentions describeChoice or aimedAt.
- Scenario 21's knownLeak "foundry-veiled-token-actor" covers only a console reading the token's actorId, which Foundry itself sends to every browser. This window shows the name in the module's own UI, with no console needed, so that known leak does not cover it.
- owner-115 item 1b lists six pickers and the Frisk's ask as what it fixed. The Call confirmation is not on that list, and its questions Q-OWN115-7 and -8 do not cover it.
- The papers record no decision that accepts this.

The one partial mitigation is the recorded Foundry limit: the actor id is in the option's value, and the token's actorId can be resolved from a console. The finding's road needs neither: a player just opens a window and presses Cancel. Under 11.3 this gives the answer away (the killer's identity), so it stays a blocker. Confidence is "read" (static): I did not run the harness, as instructed.

Support is a Hope Call with target "player". callBarred/hopeCallRefusal shut a Hope Call only in an Eclipse, under Overflow's Silence, for the dead and under the Call Silence. allowed-now.mjs's callHope road is the Eclipse alone, and a direct murder cannot open in an Eclipse (murder-rules.mjs:452), so the fight and its mask stand while Calls are open. pickTarget sends the Call to pickPlayer. The mask writes no `hidden` (maskPatch: the name, the texture, the ring, display and the flag), and E112v's veil writes no `hidden` either. The picker labels each row nameAsSeen(a), so the masked killer shows as "?", but it returns the actor itself. sheet-actions.mjs hands that choice unchanged to confirmCall. confirmCall's describeChoice reads `choice.target.name` (choice.text is unset for a player pick). The mask rewrites only the token's name and the actor's img, so the actor keeps its real name. That name is escaped and drawn as the "Aimed at" line through callWindow -> actionWindow. Neither function filters names. The only DOM-level mask hooks are secret.mjs's renderChatMessageHTML (chat cards) and anonymity.mjs's renderActorSheetV2 (sheets); neither reaches a DialogV2 window. nameAsSeen is used only in the picker. Nothing is spent before Spend, and Cancel is free. The mask exists to keep the killer's identity secret, so naming the killer gives the answer away: blocker under 11.3.

checked.why:
I followed the path the finding describes. A direct murder whose opening lands on Hope or a critical makes the primary GM run maskKiller (murder-rules.mjs:772-774). maskKiller first rewrites the killer's tokens. maskPatch (mask-gm.mjs:78-79) changes only the token's name, texture, ring, display settings and flag. It then writes one field on the Actor document: img: MASK_IMG (mask-gm.mjs:252, and :238 when a mask row was already standing). Nothing on that path changes actor.name or ownership.default.

With the default setting enforceAnonymity: true (settings.mjs:1546), every new character is created with default ownership OBSERVER (anonymity.mjs:776). So every player is allowed to list every student. The Actor document is sent to every browser, which shows the real name beside the "?" picture.

I looked for a guard that would hide the name and found none:
- Searching scripts/ and styles/ for ActorDirectory, renderActorDirectory, renderDocumentDirectory, renderSidebarTab, an actors-tab selector, entry-image or thumbnail finds no hook and no CSS that hides or filters a directory entry. The only directory rules in danganronpa.css:18568-18574 are theme colours.
- nameAsSeen (mask-gm.mjs:154-158) is used only by the module's own pickers and does not reach Foundry's list.
- The mask helpers lower no ownership, and lowerOwnership in anonymity.mjs only ever lowers to OBSERVER, never to NONE.
- The project's own records treat the list as a place the picture shows. docs/dev/e112/STATUS.md:107 marks "the Actors directory | actor.img | yes, (b)" as covered and never mentions the name beside it. The handbook (gm-handbook.en.md:1139) says the portrait wears the "?" "(the sheet, the actors' list, ...)" and also promises "Nobody but the killers is told who it is", which this contradicts.

The second sign is real too. onRenderSheet closes a sheet only when maskedSheetClosed is true (anonymity.mjs:122), and that is true only for the one masked student a player does not own. So double-clicking each entry in the list also singles the killer out.

One piece I could not check in this repository: that v14's Actors list shows an Observer each entry's img thumbnail next to its name. That is standard Foundry behaviour, and the handbook's own sentence and STATUS.md:107 assume it. Every step of the module's code I traced myself.

On severity, the "?" sits beside the killer's real name in an interface list every player can open, before the body is found. Under section 11.3 that gives the answer away, so it is a blocker.

checked.why:
The finding's road needs a player to open Foundry's Actors tab, and a player has no Actors tab. The module's stylesheet hides the whole of Foundry's sidebar for every non-GM browser, Actors directory included. The class that rule keys on is set for every non-GM at ready. The finding's search for ActorDirectory and renderActorDirectory missed this because the rule names #sidebar, not the directory. Its second tell, trying each entry in the list to see whose sheet shuts, rides the same list. A player can only open another student's sheet from that student's token, and the killer's token already shows the "?", so it names nobody.

The papers that treat the Actors list as a player surface do so without checking that CSS: E112 STATUS's table row, the handbook's parenthesis "the actors' list" and the comment in anonymity.mjs. Those are wrong text, not a working leak. Nothing in scripts/ opens ui.actors or a directory popout for a player.

The tests and papers do not pin the opposite either way. Tier 2 E112 and R7406 pin actor.img === MASK_IMG on purpose, LIVE-E112-04 (2) asks the table to check the "?" on the actor list, and known-leaks.json foundry-masked-token-actor records only the console road.

What survives is small and off this road:
- Before ready, while body.drpg-player is not yet set (module.mjs:530 in Hooks.once("ready")), a reloading player could catch Foundry's sidebar for a moment. I did not measure this.
- A sheet of the killer that a player already had open closes when the mask falls. The handbook documents this (gm-handbook.en.md:1139) and it is a separate tell.
- A different road, outside my lens and not traced to the end: the day-end board and its kept card. sequence.mjs:929 `dayBoardOf` reads name and actor.img for the whole cast. Its `portraitOf` (sequence.mjs:733-736) lets MASK_IMG through, since that path is neither mystery-man nor /icons/svg/. The board plays on the same time-of-day change that ends the mask, so whether it draws the "?" beside the killer's name depends on which runs first. That needs its own reading.

checked.why: I followed the whole path myself and found nothing on it that hides the name. (1) The GM picks the target. call-pickers.mjs pickPlayer labels each option with nameAsSeen, and nameAsSeen returns the real name on a GM, so nothing marks the masked character in the list. The pool filters out only non-students, the GM's own actor and the dead. (2) spendDespairCallFor asks only isGM, allowedNow road callDespair (Eclipse, then trial), the pool, and refusalBeforePaying / projectRefusal / gatherRefusal. None of these asks about a mask. calls.mjs, call-effects.mjs, call-world.mjs and despair.mjs have no mask reference at all. (3) Each effect writes choice.target.name or beneficiary.name into `done`: armed, hopeGranted, damaged, silenced, chained. (4) The card is posted through announce with no whisper and no veiled. In utils.mjs, privately takes the `!list?.length` branch to a plain ChatMessage.create, so postSecret and wordsFor/maskNames (secret.mjs) never run. The only chat hooks are private-rolls.mjs, sheet-audit, roll-draw, trial, safeword, spectator-ui, gm-bridge and secret.mjs drawPrivateCard. None of them reads the mask for a public card. In private-rolls the only mask use is maskSplit, for rolls. The mask helpers are used only in the pickers, frisk, listen, anonymity (sheet closing) and murder-rules maskedName. (5) The window is reachable. Direct murders declared in an Eclipse are judged after endEclipse has already advanced the time of day (eclipse.mjs: advanceTimeOfDay at 474, then judgePendingMurders at 529). So the mask opens outside an Eclipse and lasts until the next time of day, and callDespair is open for that whole time, during the incident and after it. I lowered the severity from major to minor. The card names the target ("Chie Mori loses 2 Health") but never ties that name to the "?". The finding's failure_scenario says "the table knows who the ? is", and that overstates it: a reader learns the identity only by inference, for example from a Chain or a Silence matching how the "?" token behaves. The case does not follow from the card alone. The leak also needs a GM to choose the masked killer as a Despair target in that window, which is a particular situation, not an ordinary one. It does break the owner's 14.11 rule as namesHiddenFrom states it: the masked name is cut from every card a reader outside the mask is given, and this card is not cut. It is not a blocker.

checked.why: I traced the whole road and found no guard on it. On the primary GM, stealFromPerson writes the thief's real name into the victim's card. whisperToOwner sends that card to every GM plus the victim's owners, so the GM is one of its readers. In post(), the GM's own copy is cut with wordsFor(GM), which hides nothing. remember() then stores html and lines (the uncut words) with the readers list, and keeps nothing of the mask. endMask clears the token flag (restorePatch sets it to forcedDeletion or false), so after a new time of day namesHiddenFrom answers []. When the bystander's browser is ready it calls askForWords() (also on a GM's gmReady packet). answerWordsRequest checks only the world, the author, the flag and that the asker is a reader. It then sends wordsFor(sender.id, words), and that function reads the mask as it is at that moment. secret.mjs has no other mask check: grep finds only standingMask/incidentVeils, which veil the speaker and the author. No render-time filter in scripts/ calls maskNames or namesHiddenFrom: the only other caller is frisk.mjs:839, a live packet. I did not trace every caller of updateSecret to see whether its rebuilt html carries the name, so that second road is read only in outline. The answerWordsRequest road is enough on its own. I keep the severity at major, not blocker. The card names the thief and when the theft happened, not that the thief is the killer, so the reader has to make that link themselves. It is a strong lead, but it does not give the answer outright.
